sentences.zh: 今年我一直在以一种切合实际的方式优先关注自己的健康，而让我保持高度自律和动力的秘诀，就是我的WHOOP手环。

sentences.zh: 我是一个极度看重数据的人，这就是为什么我那么喜欢WHOOP，因为它能让我真切地看明白为什么我的身体在不同日子会有不同的感觉，为什么我跑步的状态会不一样，

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供所有这些数据和模式，好让我能做出更好的决策，包括知道什么时候该放松休息，什么时候该全力以赴。

sentences.zh: 还有些人收集香水瓶、咖啡马克杯、海外纸币，或是80年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.zh: 萨姆将带领大家探索那些构成我们自身的记忆、执念与微小珍宝。

sentences.en: And welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《你二十多岁的心理学》，在这里，我们探讨二十多岁时遭遇的重大生活改变与过渡，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: Welcome back to a new episode.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听新的一期节目。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, I am so stoked to have you here for perhaps my most highly requested podcast episode of all time.
sentences.zh: 新听友们，老听友们，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，我都非常高兴你能来到这里，收听这期也许是我有史以来呼声最高的一期播客节目。

sentences.en: Every week I receive so many DMs from people who have had their hearts absolutely shattered, who have been through the worst breakup of their lives,
sentences.zh: 每周我都会收到无数私信，来自那些心碎欲绝、经历过人生中最惨烈分手的人，

sentences.en: who are grieving the end of a relationship.
sentences.zh: 来自那些正为一段关系的结束而悲伤的人。

sentences.en: And today we're going to tackle all of it.
sentences.zh: 而今天，我们要全面剖析这一切。

sentences.en: We're going to discuss the nitty-gritty science and research and psychology behind our brains and our bodies and our emotions during a breakup.
sentences.zh: 我们要深入探讨分手期间，我们的大脑、身体和情感背后那些硬核的科学、研究与心理学，

sentences.en: Why they leave such lasting emotional scars and how we can essentially move on and really begin to realize the best versions of ourselves in the midst of heartache.
sentences.zh: 探讨为什么分手会留下如此持久的情感伤疤，以及我们该如何真正释怀，并在心碎之中开始蜕变，去实现最好的自己。

sentences.en: On a personal note, those who have listened to this show for a while will know that this podcast emerged from the ruins of a relationship, one that I had in my early 20s.
sentences.zh: 说句题外话，听过这个节目一段时间的人都知道，这个播客其实是从我二十出头时的一段破碎恋情中诞生的。

sentences.en: And this show, this podcast, all that it's become, it was kind of my saviour, my little passion project that got me through a rough time and allowed me to really reclaim
sentences.zh: 而这个节目、这个播客以及它所拥有的一切，可以说是我的救赎，是我那个陪我度过艰难时期、并让我真正重新找回……

sentences.en: a lot of my identity and my independence.
sentences.zh: 找回许多自我认同与独立的精神寄托。

sentences.en: And that very ex actually came on the show a few months back.
sentences.zh: 而那位前任其实在几个月前还上了我的节目。

sentences.en: But right as I was beginning to heal from that breakup,
sentences.zh: 但就在我开始从那场分手阴影中恢复过来的时候，

sentences.en: I started seeing someone else.
sentences.zh: 我又开始和另一个人约会了。

sentences.en: I can safely say it was never very serious in the way that my previous relationship was.
sentences.zh: 我可以坦言，这段关系从来不像我之前的感情那样深刻认真。

sentences.en: I never really dreamed of marrying this person and, you know, God forbid having children with him, let alone a lease or a mortgage.
sentences.zh: 我从未真正梦想过要嫁给这个人，更别提上帝保佑还要跟他生孩子了，至于一起签租房合同或背房贷就更不用说了。

sentences.en: But when it came to an end, it crushed me.
sentences.zh: 但当它结束时，我却彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: It destroyed me in a way that for the last eight to 10 months, I really never thought I was going to recover from.
sentences.zh: 它摧毁了我的方式，让我觉得在过去的八到十个月里，我再也无法恢复过来了。

sentences.en: It's really funny how our brains take these intense romantic experiences and do not let go.
sentences.zh: 真是有趣，我们的大脑竟然会紧抓着这些强烈的情感体验不放。

sentences.en: And I spent so many weeks and months almost begging my mind to move on, to stop obsessing and thinking about all the what ifs.
sentences.zh: 我有好几个星期甚至好几个月，几乎是在祈求自己的大脑能够翻篇，别再执着于那些“如果当初”的假设胡思乱想。

sentences.en: And then the other day, a flip just kind of switched in my brain.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，我脑子里仿佛突然有一根弦被拨动了。

sentences.en: I was driving home from somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我正开车从某个地方回家。

sentences.en: I don't really remember where.
sentences.zh: 我记不清具体是哪儿了。

sentences.en: And for all of my Taylor Swift fans out there, the song Clean came on.
sentences.zh: 所有泰勒·斯威夫特的粉丝们，当时正放着那首《Clean》。

sentences.en: Honestly, number one breakup song.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这绝对是分手神曲第一名。

sentences.en: But I just had this weird epiphany where I was like, yeah,
sentences.zh: 但我当时突然有了一种奇怪的顿悟，心想：好吧，

sentences.en: I'm ready to move on now and I'm ready to make this episode.
sentences.zh: 我终于准备好翻篇了，我也准备好录制这期节目了。

sentences.en: I've read so many books.
sentences.zh: 我读了那么多的书。

sentences.en: I've done the research for my own sake.
sentences.zh: 为了自愈，我做了各种研究。

sentences.en: I've done the work, been to therapy, consulted all of my friends who would listen.
sentences.zh: 我努力过了，看过了心理医生，也咨询了所有愿意听我倾诉的朋友。

sentences.en: So let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们来聊聊这个吧。

sentences.en: And I really want to talk to my fellow
sentences.zh: 我真的很想和同龄的

sentences.en: 20-something-year-olds who are going through or have gone through the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 二十多岁的朋友们聊聊，你们正在经历或曾经经历过一模一样的事情。

sentences.en: Breakups are hard.
sentences.zh: 分手总是很难。

sentences.en: They are incredibly confusing and raw and terrible.
sentences.zh: 它们让人感到无比困惑、痛苦和糟糕。

sentences.en: But they are also such a sacred time, I think, for self-growth and personal development.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，它们同样是自我成长和个人发展的神圣时期。

sentences.en: You know, I don't believe I would be the person I am today without the formative breakups that I've gone through in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果没有在二十多岁时经历那些塑造了我的分手，我绝不会成为今天的自己。

sentences.en: They each have taught me something so unique and completely diverted my life path.
sentences.zh: 每一次分手都教给我独特的东西，并彻底改变了我的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: It's also such a common pattern of behavior to leave or exit a relationship and suddenly become, like, really obsessed with the gym or your work to find that you have more time
sentences.zh: 这也是一种非常普遍的行为模式，在结束一段关系后，突然变得对健身房或工作狂热无比，你会发现自己有了更多时间

sentences.en: for your friends and for your family and for yourself.
sentences.zh: 去陪朋友、陪家人，还有关爱自己。

sentences.en: And I believe it's because this experience presents such a pivotal time to realize the best version of yourself, even whilst we're still, you know, often hurting and grieving.
sentences.zh: 我相信这是因为这段经历提供了一个关键时期，让我们去实现最好的自己，哪怕此时此刻我们其实（你知道的）仍然在痛苦和悲伤中。

sentences.en: You know, two complex versions of ourselves, two emotional states, can exist at once.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们身上可以同时存在两种复杂的自我版本，两种情感状态。

sentences.en: So what I want to do today is break down that complexity and reveal what's really going on neurologically and psychologically when our relationships come to an end.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我想做的是，剖析这种复杂性，揭示当我们的关系走到尽头时，神经学和心理学层面究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: We are going to cover what happens to our brains in the weeks and months following a breakup, why we react the way we do, why the experience is so uniquely painful.
sentences.zh: 我们要探讨在分手后的几周和几个月里，我们的大脑会发生什么变化，为什么我们的反应会是这样，为什么这段经历会如此痛苦得独一无二。

sentences.en: We're going to discuss how we can actually apply the stages of grief to the end of a relationship and why actually sometimes it's our shorter relationships
sentences.zh: 我们要讨论如何将悲伤的各个阶段应用到一段关系的终结上，以及为什么有时候那些短暂的感情

sentences.en: that can be so much more significant.
sentences.zh: 其实反而更具深刻意义。

sentences.en: Of course, we can't talk about breakups without a discussion on heartbreak, but also how we can move on and heal.
sentences.zh: 当然，谈论分手就绕不开对心碎的讨论，还有我们该如何向前看并完成疗愈。

sentences.en: What advice does psychology have for us in those moments when we are so done with the relationship, so ready to move on, but still feel really stuck in the past and in the memories
sentences.zh: 当我们对一段关系彻底死心、准备好重新开始，却依然深深陷在过去、陷在对那个人的回忆以及曾经的点滴中无法自拔时，心理学能给我们什么建议呢？

sentences.en: of the person and what was.
sentences.zh: 致所有心碎的朋友，致那些正在康复、正在悲伤的人，这期节目就是为你准备的。

sentences.en: For my heartbroken people out there, for those on the mend, those who are grieving, this episode is for you.
sentences.zh: 我曾亲历过，我懂你的痛，我想把那些我当初多么希望自己能早点知道的指引和建议分享给你。

sentences.en: I've been there, I know your pain, and I want to give you the guidance and the advice that I so wished that I'd had earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以，废话不多说，让我们来剖析分手的心理学、心碎的心理学，以及如何疗愈、如何绽放、如何放手。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's break down the psychology of breakups, the psychology of heartbreak, and how to heal, how to flourish, how to let go.
sentences.zh: 我认为，对于我们这些二十多岁的人来说，心碎是一种普遍的经历。

sentences.en: I think that heartbreak is a universal experience for those of us in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 我们在这个十年里约会，摸索自己的喜好，轻松随意地坠入爱河，坚信这些伴侣就是我们一生的挚爱。

sentences.en: We spend this decade dating and figuring out what we like, falling in love so effortlessly and carelessly, believing that these characters are the loves of our lives.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，一切都结束了。

sentences.en: And then one day, it's all over.
sentences.zh: 无论你是提出分手的那个人，还是被分手的那个人，双方都只能留下来收拾残局。

sentences.en: And whether you were the one who ended things or not, both parties are left picking up the pieces.
sentences.zh: 这是一段极其震撼的经历，有时甚至能改变一生，而且绝对刻骨铭心。

sentences.en: It's an incredibly powerful experience, sometimes life-changing, always memorable.
sentences.zh: 我想，证据就是我们对关系的终结是如此着迷。

sentences.en: I think evidence of that is how fascinated we are by the end of relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在谈论它，和朋友们讨论它，人们在经历了一次糟糕的分手后写出了有史以来最伟大的几首歌曲。

sentences.en: We talk about it all the time, we discuss it with our friends, people write some of the greatest songs of all time on the back of a bad breakup.
sentences.zh: 整个电影、书籍和电视剧流派都是以痛苦和心碎为前提创作的，因为情感甚至是身体上的冲击

sentences.en: Entire genres of movies and books and televisions is created on the premise of heartache and heartbreak because the emotional and even physical impact
sentences.zh: 是如此深远而重大。

sentences.en: is so profound and significant.
sentences.zh: 那么，在一段关系结束时，我们的大脑究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: So what exactly goes on in our brains at the end of a relationship?
sentences.zh: 我认为人类的连接是极其美妙的，还有爱。

sentences.en: I think human connection is incredibly beautiful and, you know, love.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是世间最美好的感觉之一。

sentences.en: Well, that's one of the best feelings out there.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至会争辩说，被人看见、被人关爱、被人理解，就是我们生存的全部意义。

sentences.en: Some would really argue it's our entire reason for being to be seen by someone else and cared for and understood.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我不仅希望这是每个人的经历，它也确实改变了我们大脑诠释世界的方式。

sentences.en: Well, not only do I hope that that's been everyone's experience, but it really does change how our brain interprets the world.
sentences.zh: 俗话说爱是一种毒品，但这其实不仅仅是一个比喻。

sentences.en: The saying goes that love is a drug, but it's actually not just a saying.
sentences.zh: 它完全是事实。

sentences.en: It's very much true.
sentences.zh: 坠入爱河会释放大量强效的神经递质和化学物质，比如多巴胺、血清素、催产素，所有这些对于快乐、激情、

sentences.en: Falling in love releases so many powerful neurotransmitters and chemicals like dopamine, like serotonin, like oxytocin, all of which are really important for pleasure and passion,
sentences.zh: 羁绊以及其他强烈的情感都至关重要。

sentences.en: bonding and other intense feelings.
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现，强烈的浪漫爱情对大脑的影响，与强效药物对大脑的影响如出一辙。

sentences.en: Researchers have found that intense feelings of romantic love affect the brain in the same way in the same way as powerful drugs.
sentences.zh: 这位教授，

sentences.en: This professor,
sentences.zh: 海伦·费舍尔博士（Dr. Helen Fisher），她是一位人类学家和恋爱研究员，她针对我们的大脑化学反应与爱的感觉之间的这种相互作用进行了一系列研究。

sentences.en: Dr. Helen Fisher, she's an anthropologist and a relationship researcher, she conducted a series of studies on this very interaction between our brain chemistry and the feeling
sentences.zh: 具体来说，她发现当我们坠入爱河时起作用的化学物质——也就是海量的多巴胺和血清素——以及活跃的大脑通路和结构，

sentences.en: of love.
sentences.zh: 和我们享受可卡因带来的快感时简直一模一样。

sentences.en: Specifically, she found that the same chemicals, that is, massive amounts of dopamine and serotonin, are in play and many of the same brain pathways and structures are active
sentences.zh: 我们都知道像可卡因这样的非法药物具有极强的成瘾性，而我们可以合乎逻辑地推断，既然爱激活了许多相同的神经反应，它也是一样的。

sentences.en: when we are falling in love as when we are enjoying a cocaine high.
sentences.zh: 你可能甚至亲自感受过那种强大的效应，或者我们称之为由大脑中化学物质的涌入和冲击所带来的“玫瑰色滤镜”。

sentences.en: And we all know that illegal drugs like cocaine are incredibly addictive and we can logic that love, given it activates many of the same neurological reactions, is the same.
sentences.zh: 那么，当爱的源泉——通常是我们的关系、来自对方的肯定以及那种温暖美妙的感觉——走向终结时，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: You've probably even felt those powerful effects or, you know, the rose-tinted glasses, as we call it, that are brought on by this influx and this rush of chemicals in our brain.
sentences.zh: 这是一个悲伤的现实，我们从每天和那个人聊天、与他们分享成功的喜悦、分担失败和痛苦（你知道的，我们了解他们的一切），

sentences.en: So, what happens when that source of our love, often our relationship and the validation and the warm gooey feelings comes to an end?
sentences.zh: 到这一切结束时，本质上我们的大脑进入了戒断期。

sentences.en: It's a sad reality, you know, we go from talking to that person every day, from celebrating our successes with them and mourning our losses and our failures, you know, we know
sentences.zh: 你已经花了好几个月、甚至过去五年（无论时间有多长）去接受这种刺激以及这些强效神经递质的释放，

sentences.en: everything about them and when that's over, essentially our brain goes into withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 然后这一切戛然而止，大脑开始手忙脚乱地寻找替代品，试图重新建立那种稳态和正常感。

sentences.en: You've spent, you know, the last six months, the last five years, however long it may be, receiving that stimulation and the release of these powerful neurotransmitters
sentences.zh: 因此，在分手后，特别是如果你彻底断联（我绝对推荐这样做，我们稍后会详细谈），你的大脑基本上会进入一种急剧渴望的状态，

sentences.en: , and then it drops off and the brain is left scrambling for more, trying to re-establish that sense of homeostasis and normalcy.
sentences.zh: 这使得我们很难把注意力集中在除了那个让我们思念的人之外的任何事情上。

sentences.en: So, post-breakup, especially if you go no contact, which I would definitely recommend and we'll talk about that later, but your brain enters basically a state of acute wanting
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种与愉悦感、幸福感相关的神经递质的相对缺乏，以及对那个人的思念，甚至会引发类似临床抑郁症或戒断反应的症状，

sentences.en: and it makes it really difficult for us to focus on anything other than that person that we're missing.
sentences.zh: 这就是“爱情戒断假说”。

sentences.en: In fact, this relative kind of deficit in the neurotransmitters associated with pleasurable feelings and happiness, but also with that person, it can even give rise to symptoms
sentences.zh: 它解释了为什么我们在分手后的几个月里，会像对毒品一样疯狂渴望这个人。

sentences.en: that resemble clinical depression or withdrawal and that is the love withdrawal hypothesis.

sentences.zh: 走回头路，并开始考虑这是否是一个正确的决定。

sentences.en: This is where bargaining enters the breakup equation, with thoughts like, you know, if we get back together, I promise that I'll be a better person, or I'll go to the gym, they'll
sentences.zh: 这就是讨价还价进入分手方程式的时候，脑海中会出现这样的想法：“如果我们复合，我保证我会成为一个更好的人”，或者“我会去健身房，他们会

sentences.en: want me back.
sentences.zh: 回心转意”。

sentences.en: Bargaining comes from a feeling of helplessness, and it gives us a perceived sense of control over the situation, regardless of whether you actually were the one to end the
sentences.zh: 讨价还价源于一种无助感，它让我们对局势产生了一种幻觉般的掌控感，无论实际上是不是你主动结束了

sentences.en: relationship or not.
sentences.zh: 这段关系。

sentences.en: Sometimes we get to this point of feeling like everything was our fault, and that we want to go back.
sentences.zh: 有时我们会走到这一步，觉得一切都是自己的错，并且想要回到过去。

sentences.en: We want to change our emotional state.
sentences.zh: 我们想要改变自己的情感状态。

sentences.en: We don't want to experience this pain anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不想再经历这种痛苦了。

sentences.en: We might look back at our interactions with that person and realize all the times that maybe we were in the wrong, think that we can't do better, and you know, sometimes we
sentences.zh: 我们可能会回顾自己与那个人的互动，意识到所有那些可能自己做错了的时候，觉得自己找不到更好的了，你知道的，有时我们

sentences.en: do get back with this person, but the chances are that if you're listening to this episode, that has not been the case.
sentences.zh: 确实会和这个人复合，但如果你在听这一集，大概率情况并非如此。

sentences.en: And I saw this amazing quote the other day for all my people who and my friends who are in the bargaining stage, if there was a reason that you broke up in the
sentences.zh: 前几天我看到了一句精彩绝伦的名言，送给所有处于讨价还价阶段的人和朋友们：既然当初分手是有原因的，那么不复合也同样有原因。

sentences.en: first place, there's a reason why you shouldn't get back together.
sentences.zh: 最初，你之所以不应该复合是有原因的。

sentences.en: Like, you have to really place yourself in that logical state of mind, as hard as it is.
sentences.zh: 就像，你必须真正让自己进入那种理性的心态，尽管这很难。

sentences.en: There was a reason that relationship didn't work, and that reason is a strong enough reason to not contemplate getting back together with them.
sentences.zh: 这段关系走不下去是有原因的，而那个原因就足以成为不考虑与他们复合的充足理由。

sentences.en: And I think that's where we move on to the next stage, which is depression.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我们进入下一个阶段的时候，也就是抑郁。

sentences.en: I have this theory that this stage of the breakup, the depression stage, is really what people envision when we talk about heartache, or we talk about a breakup.
sentences.zh: 我有一种理论，分手的这个阶段——抑郁阶段，才是人们在谈论心碎或分手时真正想象的情景。

sentences.en: It's the misery, it's the 2am tears, the long drives in your car, the breakup playlist, waiting for a text back, the pain, all the hard stuff, all the difficult emotions.
sentences.zh: 那种痛苦，凌晨两点的眼泪，在车里的长途驾驶，分手播放列表，等待回信的煎熬，所有的痛苦，所有艰难的情绪。

sentences.en: During our experience of processing grief, there comes a time when all of our emotions and our imaginations and our bargaining begins to slow down, and we start
sentences.zh: 在我们经历悲伤消化的过程中，总会有一个时刻，我们所有的情绪、想象和讨价还价开始放缓，我们开始

sentences.en: to really understand the state and the situation that we're in, and kind of what we're faced with, which is that this person is no longer part of your life.
sentences.zh: 真正理解我们所处的国家和处境，以及我们即将面临的现实，那就是这个人不再是你生命中的一部分了。

sentences.en: And that's something that you really have to accept.
sentences.zh: 这是你必须真正接受的事情。

sentences.en: So in this stage of the breakup, I think we really start to feel that reality a lot more abundantly.
sentences.zh: 所以在分手的这个阶段，我认为我们开始更充分地感受到那种现实。

sentences.en: And as we begin to contemplate questions like, will I ever see this person again?
sentences.zh: 当我们开始琢磨这样一些问题：我还能再见到这个人吗？

sentences.en: Or who am I if they're not in my life?
sentences.zh: 或者如果他们不在我的生活中，我是谁？

sentences.en: Will I ever experience love again?
sentences.zh: 我还能再体验到爱吗？

sentences.en: All of those really existential questions.
sentences.zh: 所有这些非常存在主义的问题。

sentences.en: Our circumstances begin to become a lot more clear, and our loss becomes a lot more unavoidable, and that sadness grows.
sentences.zh: 我们的处境变得更加清晰，我们的失落变得更加无法逃避，悲伤也随之加剧。

sentences.en: And I think that's when the actual hard work and the healing really begins.
sentences.zh: 我想，真正的苦功和真正的治愈也正是在那时开始的。

sentences.en: In my most recent breakup, it was so strange.
sentences.zh: 在我最近的一次分手经历中，情况非常诡异。

sentences.en: I spent like the first four months being totally cool, totally okay.
sentences.zh: 我花了大概前四个月时间表现得完全无所谓，完全ok。

sentences.en: I was like, wow, this is the easiest thing I've ever done.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，哇，这是我有生以来经历过最轻松的事。

sentences.en: I'm so over this.
sentences.zh: 我已经彻底放下了。

sentences.en: And then it just all crumbled in like a minute.
sentences.zh: 然后这一切在短短一分钟内彻底崩塌。

sentences.en: There was like this one day where this, I just could feel myself entering this stage, and I just was like, oh my god, this is where it begins.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我能感觉到自己正在进入这个阶段，当时我就想：“天哪，一切才刚刚开始。”

sentences.en: I think it's important to note that the length and the intenseness of this stage is different for everyone, because we each have different pre-existing attachment
sentences.zh: 我认为重要的一点是，这个阶段的持续时间和强度对每个人来说都是不同的，因为我们每个人都有着不同的既有依恋

sentences.en: styles, temperaments, and personalities.
sentences.zh: 风格、气质和性格。

sentences.en: There are people out there who can disconnect from a relationship just like that, and who appear to move on really quickly.
sentences.zh: 有些人可以瞬间从一段感情中抽离出来，并且看起来走出来得非常快。

sentences.en: And if you're a sensitive person like me, sometimes that can really be the hardest part, knowing that the other person has moved on while you're still grieving, and trying to
sentences.zh: 如果你像我一样是个敏感的人，有时候这真的是最痛苦的部分，明知对方已经放下了，而你还在悲伤，

sentences.en: process your emotions.
sentences.zh: 试图消化自己的情绪。

sentences.en: It's almost like a competition, like who can move on the fastest, and when you're losing, it just feels really terrible.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像是一场比赛，看谁能最快放下，而当你处于落后的一方时，感觉真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: It really makes us question whether what you had was real.
sentences.zh: 这真的会让我们怀疑你们曾经拥有的感情是否真实。

sentences.en: I promise you that it was.
sentences.zh: 我向你们保证，那是真的。

sentences.en: Let me just say, if someone has appeared to move on, especially straight into a new relationship, I promise you, I promise you that they haven't moved on, and they will be
sentences.zh: 我只想说，如果有人看起来已经放下了，特别是直接进入了一段新感情，我向你们保证，我向你们保证他们根本没有放下，他们要么

sentences.en: either single in five months, or, you know, will have to deal with the repercussions in their new relationship, it's not going to be smooth sailing.
sentences.zh: 在五个月后恢复单身，要么必须应对他们在新感情中的后果，这绝不会是一帆风顺的。

sentences.en: The amount of people that I've dated who have started seeing someone like two months after we've broken up, and then like a year later have like come crawling back is
sentences.zh: 我约会过很多人，他们在我们分手大约两个月后就开始和别人交往，然后大约一年后又像狗皮膏药一样爬回来，

sentences.en: astounding, because you can't undo a relationship with the click of your fingers, you're using someone else as a distraction, and if you haven't taken the time to properly
sentences.zh: 这种数量惊人，因为你不可能打个响指就抹杀掉一段感情，你只是在把别人当成转移注意力的工具；如果你没有花时间好好去

sentences.en: journey through the stages of grief, if you've skipped past that essential emotional work, you haven't accepted what's happened, and you haven't fully processed your emotions
sentences.zh: 经历悲伤的各个阶段，如果你跳过了那些必不可少的情感功课，你没有接受所发生的事，也没有彻底消化你的情绪

sentences.en: or what that relationship meant to you.
sentences.zh: 或是那段感情对你的意义。

sentences.en: So essentially what ends up happening is you use someone else as a distraction from the hard feelings, five months later, six months later, you're back at square one.
sentences.zh: 所以最终发生的结果就是，你把另一个人当成逃避痛苦感受的工具，五个月后，六个月后，你又回到了原点。

sentences.en: I think what I'm essentially trying to say is that these individuals, they skip over all the important parts, and they don't process your emotions, they don't process their
sentences.zh: 我想表达的本质是，这些人跳过了所有重要的部分，他们没有处理自己的情绪，他们没有处理

sentences.en: emotions, and they just assume that they've reached acceptance, and acceptance of course is the final stage.
sentences.zh: 彼此的情绪，只是自以为已经达到了接受的阶段，而接受当然是最后一个阶段。

sentences.en: If you've moved through all those other stages, like this isn't a pass-go situation, you have to go through it, you have to go through the trenches.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经经历过了所有其他的阶段——这不是那种可以免除的局面，你必须经历它，你必须蹚过这些泥潭。

sentences.en: When we come to a place of acceptance, it's not that we no longer miss the person, that we no longer feel pain, all that sadness and regret can still be present in this
sentences.zh: 当我们来到接受的境界时，并不是说我们不再想念这个人，不再感到痛苦，所有的悲伤和遗憾在这个阶段

sentences.en: phase, but you also start to feel at peace, you rationally come back to yourself, you accept that it is, you know, it is what it is, that it happened for a reason, that it
sentences.zh: 依然可以存在，但你也会开始感到内心平静，理智地找回自我，接受这一切，你知道的，事已至此，一切发生都有它的原因，

sentences.en: needed to happen, you made the right choice, and you start looking forward, and maybe even dating again, but also more importantly, you forgive yourself because you're now
sentences.zh: 它必须发生，你做了正确的选择，你开始向前看，甚至再次开始约会，但更重要的是，你原谅了自己，因为你现在

sentences.en: able to accurately reflect on the relationship and see what went wrong.
sentences.zh: 能够准确地反思这段感情，并看出哪里出了问题。

sentences.en: At this stage, I think reconciliation is possible, but a warning to the wise.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，我认为破镜重圆是可能的，但要忠告大家一句。

sentences.en: I honestly don't think that you can be friends with your ex, I don't think that reconciliation will work in most cases, and like I said before, if you've been around for a
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不认为你能和前任做朋友，在大多数情况下，复合是不会成功的，就像我之前说过的，如果你关注我

sentences.en: while, you'll know that I did an episode on can exes be friends featuring my ex-boyfriend.
sentences.zh: 一段时间，你就会知道我曾做过一期关于“前任能否做朋友”的节目，嘉宾就是我的前男友。

sentences.en: And let me just say that at the time, I had a really positive outlook in that episode, but we're actually no longer friends.
sentences.zh: 请允许我这么说，当时我在那期节目中抱有非常积极的看法，但实际上我们现在已经不再是朋友了。

sentences.en: I always thought that it would be possible, but it's actually really hard to forget what you once were to each other.
sentences.zh: 我总是以为这是可能的，但要忘记你们曾经对彼此而言意味着什么，真的太难了。

sentences.en: Romantic attraction, physical attraction may fade, but our bodies and our minds remember, and if both individuals are not on the same page, it is never going to work.
sentences.zh: 浪漫的吸引力、身体的吸引力可能会消退，但我们的身体和心灵会记住，如果双方不在同一个频次上，这是永远行不通的。

sentences.en: You need to be completely and brutally honest with yourself.
sentences.zh: 你需要对你自己完全、残酷地诚实。

sentences.en: If there is even the slightest desire to get back together with this person, you're not ready.
sentences.zh: 如果哪怕存在一丝一毫想和这个人复合的渴望，你都还没准备好。

sentences.en: You're not ready to reach out, you're not ready for the closer conversation, you're not ready to talk.
sentences.zh: 你还没准备好联系对方，你还没准备好进行最后的对话，你还没准备好交谈。

sentences.en: I hope this has kind of given you guys a bit of an insight into the hidden mechanisms of our pain.
sentences.zh: 我希望这能让大家对我们痛苦的隐藏机制有一点深入的了解。

sentences.en: Regardless of what stage you're in, heartache is never easy.
sentences.zh: 无论你处于哪个阶段，心碎从来都不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: So if you're listening to this for some sage psychological wisdom on how to move on and fully let go, you are in luck because that is what I want to talk about
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你正在收听这期节目，想寻找一些关于如何放下并彻底释怀的明智心理学建议，那你有福了，因为这正是我接下来

sentences.en: next in just a
sentences.zh: 马上要谈的

sentences.en: moment.
sentences.zh: 内容。

sentences.en: Here is the brutal honest truth.
sentences.zh: 这就是残酷而诚实的真相。

sentences.en: If you want to truly let go of someone after the end of a relationship, you need to disconnect from them entirely.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在感情结束后真正放下一个人的话，你需要彻底切断与他们的联系。

sentences.en: It can be really easy to keep touching base, you know, seeing each other after things have ended, but I promise you that will only elongate the process of emotional and
sentences.zh: 保持联络可能会非常容易，你知道的，在事情结束后还互相关照、见见面，但我向你们保证，这只会拉长情感和

sentences.en: physical detachment.
sentences.zh: 身体脱离的过程。

sentences.en: All of the science and the psychology says that the months after a breakup are in essence a period of withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 所有的科学和心理学都表明，分手后的几个月本质上就是一个戒断期。

sentences.en: You're trying to eliminate your brain's addiction to this person and the feeling that they bring you, but if you keep finding ways to see them, sleeping with them,
sentences.zh: 你正在试图戒掉大脑对这个人的依赖以及他们带给你的感觉，但如果你一直找机会见他们、与他们发生性关系、

sentences.en: talking, you give your brain what we call invariable variable reward or reinforcement, which only promotes the obsession and the difficulty in breaking things off completely.
sentences.zh: 交谈，你就会给大脑提供我们所说的不定常变量奖励或强化，这只会助长执念，并增加彻底斩断情丝的难度。

sentences.en: Every time you see your ex, especially in a manner that is reminiscent of your past romantic relationship, your brain receives a dopamine hit and it reinforces that
sentences.zh: 每次你见到前任，尤其是以那种让你回忆起过去浪漫关系的方式见面时，你的大脑就会获得一剂多巴胺，并强化这种

sentences.en: pathway or learned conditioning between this person and the warm, fuzzy feelings that we receive.
sentences.zh: 通路或习得的条件反射，将这个人与我们得到的温暖、美妙的感觉联系起来。

sentences.en: I hate to say it, I know it's not always a popular opinion, but no contact truly is your friend if your aim is to let go, if your aim is to move on.
sentences.zh: 我不愿意这么说，我知道这可能不是一个受欢迎的观点，但如果你想放手，如果你想往前走，不联系真的是你最好的朋友。

sentences.en: From my own personal experience, I know that decision is a lot harder than the easier path of kind of keeping in touch, but I promise you in three months time you will be thanking
sentences.zh: 从我个人的经验来看，我知道这个决定比选择保持联络那条轻松的路要难得多，但我向你保证，三个月后你会感谢

sentences.en: yourself because it's important to remember that breakups aren't just social, they're not just emotional, they are neurological and your brain is the basis of your
sentences.zh: 自己的，因为必须记住，分手不仅是社交层面的，不仅是情感层面的，它们是神经学层面的，而你的大脑正是你对这个人产生

sentences.en: attachment and your obsession with this person.
sentences.zh: 依恋和执念的基础。

sentences.en: So if you break the habit, you'll find that you'll heal quicker.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你打破这个习惯，你会发现自己能更快地痊愈。

sentences.en: Block their number and follow them right now.
sentences.zh: 立刻拉黑他们的电话号码并取关他们。

sentences.en: You don't need to see what they're doing, you don't need to see what parties they're attending, what people they're with.
sentences.zh: 你不需要看他们在做什么，你不需要看他们参加了什么派对，他们和什么人在一起。

sentences.en: It's like scratching an itch.
sentences.zh: 这就像是去抓一个发痒的蚊子包。

sentences.en: It may feel good, but the sting will only come back stronger later.
sentences.zh: 这感觉可能不错，但以后痛苦只会变本加厉地袭来。

sentences.en: No contact is your friend, as hard as it may be.
sentences.zh: 不管有多难，不联系绝对是你的好朋友。

sentences.en: We know from research that the end of a relationship causes a plunge in dopamine and serotonin levels, hence why we often enter, I think, a pretty dark state in many ways that kind
sentences.zh: 研究表明，一段关系的结束会导致多巴胺和血清素水平骤降，这就是为什么我们经常会陷入我觉得在很多方面相当黑暗的状态，这种状态

sentences.en: of mimics even the symptoms of depression.
sentences.zh: 甚至有点像抑郁症的症状。

sentences.en: Additionally, I think exposure to our past memories with someone and their images or thoughts of them, it activates some of the very same brain regions that interpret and
sentences.zh: 此外，我认为接触我们过去和某人的回忆、他们的照片或对他们的思念，会激活大脑中某些与解读和

sentences.en: process physical pain like we talked about before.
sentences.zh: 处理身体疼痛相同的区域，就像我们之前讨论过的那样。

sentences.en: So how do we minimize these physiological symptoms that often draw us back into connecting with our exes?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何将这些常常把我们拉回与前任复合的生理症状降到最低呢？

sentences.en: You need to find a source of dopamine and happiness that has absolutely nothing to do with that person.
sentences.zh: 你需要找到一个与那个人毫无关系的、能产生多巴胺和快乐的源泉。

sentences.en: You need to find a replacement for the deficit that they've left you in.
sentences.zh: 你需要为他们留给你的空缺找到替代品。

sentences.en: And it's kind of up to you, but I would say something like watching TV or napping, that's a temporary fix.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上取决于你，但我会说像看电视或小睡这样的事情，只是权宜之计。

sentences.en: What we want is an activity that creates long-term gratification.
sentences.zh: 我们想要的是能带来长期满足感的活动。

sentences.en: One of my friends got super into doing triathlons and rock climbing after she split from her partner.
sentences.zh: 我的一个朋友在和伴侣分开后，变得超级热衷于铁人三项和攀岩。

sentences.en: She was honestly so jacked by the end of it, but it was also something that really gave her a sense of purpose and a sense of self beyond the relationship.
sentences.zh: 老实说，到最后她身材练得超棒，但这也是一件真正赋予她目标感以及超越这段关系的自我意识的事情。

sentences.en: Something like joining a sports club, a social sports team, an art class, gardening, miniature trains, you know, honestly, it doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 比如加入体育俱乐部、社交运动队、艺术班、园艺、微型火车，你知道，说实话，这其实并不重要。

sentences.en: As long as it makes you happy and crucially, you're able to enter a flow state, a state of complete calm and focus and excitement when you're participating.
sentences.zh: 只要它能让你快乐，最关键的是，当你在参与时，你能进入心流状态——一种完全平静、专注和兴奋的状态。

sentences.en: That is what's most important, that you're able to reconnect with yourself, you're able to increase those dopamine levels without needing the other person.
sentences.zh: 这才是最重要的，你能重新与自己建立联系，无需依赖另一个人就能提高多巴胺水平。

sentences.en: But I would also say bonus points if it involves being able to meet new people and hopefully new friends who have no idea who your ex is, who are not friends with your
sentences.zh: 但我也想说，如果这能让你结识新的人，并且希望是那些完全不知道你的前任是谁、不是你前任的朋友、

sentences.en: ex, who only know you as yourself.
sentences.zh: 只把你当作你自己的人，那就更加分了。

sentences.en: I think one of the major difficulties, you know, moving on from a relationship is how conflated our individual identities become with someone else's.
sentences.zh: 我认为从一段关系中走出来的一个主要困难，你知道的，在于我们个体的身份与别人的身份交织得有多深。

sentences.en: So finding new people, new hobbies, new facets of yourself that have absolutely nothing to do with that other person, it really does help aid your healing journey and reconnect you
sentences.zh: 所以寻找新的人、新的爱好、你身上与另一个人毫无关系的崭新面孔，确实有助于推动你的疗愈之旅，让你重新连接

sentences.en: with your essence, with your personal sense of identity and with your own self-worth and your own value.
sentences.zh: 你的本质、你的个人身份感以及你自己的自尊和自我价值。

sentences.en: A lot of these tips may sound like avoidance or distraction, you know, cutting off your ex completely, diving into your new sport and your new friendships, but there is something
sentences.zh: 很多这样的建议听起来可能像是逃避或转移注意力，你知道的，彻底切断与前任的联系，全身心投入到你的新运动和新友情中，但其中有一点

sentences.en: really important about just allowing yourself to feel self-pity and to wallow.
sentences.zh: 真的非常重要，那就是允许自己顾影自怜和沉溺其中。

sentences.en: The people I know who try really hard to pretend like they're alright and move on really quickly, you know, four months later they're the ones who suffer the most and who hurt the
sentences.zh: 我认识那些拼命装作自己很好、很快就走出来的人，你知道的，四个月后他们反而是痛苦最深、受伤

sentences.en: longest because suppression, which is what they're doing, is an unhealthy coping mechanism and all it does is prolong the inevitable.
sentences.zh: 最久的人，因为压抑（也就是他们正在做的事）是一种不健康的应对机制，它唯一的作用就是延长必然要面对的痛苦。

sentences.en: You need to break down, you need to cry, you need to wish you'd never met them and swear to your friends you'll never date again.
sentences.zh: 你需要崩溃，你需要哭泣，你需要希望自己从未遇到过他们，并向朋友发誓再也不约会了。

sentences.en: Trust me, it's a rite of passage to really feel your emotions.
sentences.zh: 相信我，真正去感受自己的情绪是成长必经的一道关卡。

sentences.en: You know, you don't need to get lost in it, it's all with moderation, but I think importantly while you're going through this, make sure you create a safe space to really feel what
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不需要迷失其中，一切都要适度，但我认为重要的是，在你经历这个过程时，确保创造一个安全的空间去真正感受

sentences.en: you're feeling, to really, like I said, wallow.
sentences.zh: 你的感受，就像我说的，去好好沉溺吧。

sentences.en: I do this thing where every time a relationship ends, I go to Queensland, which is where I kind of grew up and it's where I feel most vulnerable and I know there that I
sentences.zh: 我有个习惯，每当一段关系结束，我就会去昆士兰，那是我长大的地方，也是我感觉最脆弱的地方，在那里我知道自己

sentences.en: am safe, that I am able to really express myself, I'm able to feel my emotions, there's no one I need to keep up with, I'm not going to run into them anywhere and it
sentences.zh: 是安全的，我能够真正地表达自己，我能够感受自己的情绪，没有人需要我去迎合，我也不会在任何地方偶遇他们，这

sentences.en: can be something as simple as rearranging your room to kind of disassociate from the memories you might have with them in there.
sentences.zh: 可以很简单，比如重新布置你的房间，从而与你在那里和他们共同拥有的回忆产生一点距离。

sentences.en: Go and buy yourself a cosy breakup blanket or a candle, create a little oasis for yourself to be vulnerable and to be emotional and give yourself time to endure the pain.
sentences.zh: 去给自己买一条舒适的分手毯或一支蜡烛，为自己打造一个小绿洲，去展露脆弱、释放情感，给自己时间去熬过痛苦。

sentences.en: I know it's so much easier to distract, to flee, to run away from hard emotions but I think that you'll be surprised how much you will learn about yourself because emotional
sentences.zh: 我知道转移注意力、逃避、逃离痛苦的情绪要容易得多，但我认为你会惊讶于自己能学到多少关于自己的东西，因为情感

sentences.en: release brings clarity.
sentences.zh: 释放会带来清晰的思路。

sentences.en: I also think it's really important to give yourself the closure that you need.
sentences.zh: 我也认为给自己所需要的释怀（closure）非常重要。

sentences.en: I think where people often go wrong as they try and move on from someone is believing that only the other person can bring them closure and I don't believe that for a second.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们在试图从某人身边走出来时常常犯的错误，是相信只有另一个人才能带给自己释怀，我一秒钟都不信这个。

sentences.en: Ask yourself, if you're thinking about reaching out, if you're thinking about having the closure conversation with them, what exactly are you looking for when you're talking
sentences.zh: 问问你自己，如果你在考虑联系对方，如果你在考虑和他们进行那场关于释怀的对话，当你在谈论

sentences.en: about closure?
sentences.zh: 释怀时，你到底在寻找什么？

sentences.en: Is there really a specific thing that they can give you or they can say that's going to make you feel better?
sentences.zh: 真的有什么具体的事是他们能给你的，或者他们能说出口的，能让你感觉好一点的吗？

sentences.en: The answer is probably not and even if there is, it's very unlikely that they're actually going to say it.
sentences.zh: 答案很可能没有，即使有，他们真正说出口的可能性也非常小。

sentences.en: Here's the truth, you can give yourself the closure that you need.
sentences.zh: 这就是真相，你可以自己给自己所需要的释怀。

sentences.en: They are not responsible for healing you, that's your job and there are a few ways that you can kind of activate that closing of the chapter, ways that you can pursue full body and
sentences.zh: 他们不负责治愈你，那是你的工作，有几种方法你可以用来启动那个章节的关闭，通过这些方式你可以从上一段感情中寻求身心和

sentences.en: emotional closure from your previous relationship.
sentences.zh: 情感上的彻底释怀。

sentences.en: The one I always suggest is to write a letter to that person.
sentences.zh: 我一直建议的方法是给那个人写一封信。

sentences.en: Just get a couple pieces of paper, I want you to write everything that you loved about them, everything that was special but also why you're mad, why you're angry, why
sentences.zh: 拿几张纸，我要你写下你喜欢他们的一切、所有特别的地方，但也要写下你为什么疯狂、为什么生气、为什么

sentences.en: you're miserable.
sentences.zh: 你痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: Talk about how you feel right now but also why you need to let go.
sentences.zh: 谈谈你现在的感受，但也谈谈你为什么要放手。

sentences.en: Consider it almost a final love letter to them, all of the emotions that you're feeling, put it on the page and then I want you to put it away and I also don't want you to
sentences.zh: 把它当成写给他们的最后一封情书，把你所有的情绪都倾注在纸上，然后我要你把它收起来，而且我要你

sentences.en: stop writing until you've really, you're really done, you've really exhausted all the thoughts in your brain and either get rid of that letter or keep it in a box, don't send it to
sentences.zh: 写到真正写完、真正榨干脑海中的所有想法时才停下来，要么把那封信扔掉，要么把它放在盒子里，不要发给

sentences.en: them, don't tell anyone about it, just do it for you, say goodbye in your own way.
sentences.zh: 他们，不要告诉任何人，只为你自己去做，以你自己的方式好好告别。

sentences.en: I also want you to remove anything that reminds you of them from your physical space.
sentences.zh: 我还想让你把任何能让你想起他们的东西从你的物理空间中移除。

sentences.en: All that's going to do is reactivate those synaptic connections in your brain that make you want them back, that make you long and obsess.
sentences.zh: 这样做只会重新激活你大脑中那些让你想要他们回来、让你渴望和执念的突触连接。

sentences.en: It's really important to recreate or refurbish or clean your personal spaces of memories of them so that you can reclaim them as your own.
sentences.zh: 重新布置、翻新或清理你个人空间中关于他们的回忆非常重要，这样你才能把这些空间重新夺回，变成你自己的。

sentences.en: If you're really struggling and you're like, I really want to reach out to this person, no contact isn't working, I miss them, they are the love of my life, visualization is
sentences.zh: 如果你真的很挣扎，心想：我真的好想联系这个人，不联系这一招不管用，我想念他们，他们是我一生的挚爱，那么可视化（想象）

sentences.en: your friend.
sentences.zh: 就是你的好朋友。

sentences.en: I want you to visualize yourself burying a box containing all the memories from that relationship and if that thought comes in where you're like, I can't stop thinking
sentences.zh: 我要你想象自己正在埋下一个盒子，里面装满了那段关系中的所有回忆，如果那个念头冒出来，比如：我满脑子都是

sentences.en: about this person, I can't stop obsessing over them, one of my friends gave me an amazing strategy for this.
sentences.zh: 这个人，我无法停止对他们的执念，我的一个朋友为此给了我一个绝妙的策略。

sentences.en: Imagine their face on a ball and then picture yourself hitting that ball as far away as possible.
sentences.zh: 想象他们的脸印在一个球上，然后想象自己把那个球击得越远越好。

sentences.en: It really helps.
sentences.zh: 这真的很管用。

sentences.en: I will say that I have used that a few times and visualization is a great way of kind of tricking your brain into creating a reality that it wants.
sentences.zh: 我得说我用过好几次，可视化真是欺骗大脑去创造它想要的现实的好方法。

sentences.en: I think it's also important, you know, with that letter idea that we suggested to make peace with the past but accept the future.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，你知道的，结合我们建议的写信的主意，与过去讲和但接受未来是很重要的。

sentences.en: They're no longer going to be in your life, that's a really hard pill to swallow.
sentences.zh: 他们将不再出现在你的生活中，这是一个很难接受的现实。

sentences.en: But write out all of your favorite things about them on a piece of paper and then for each reason I want you to write down the reasons why you needed to break up, the
sentences.zh: 但在纸上写下你喜欢他们所有的点，然后针对每一个理由，我要你写下你需要分手的理由、

sentences.en: reasons why you couldn't stay, why this breakup is necessary.

sentences.zh: 有时我认为在浮出水面之前更深入地了解兽穴是件重要的事，提醒自己外面有更好的爱在等着你，而你愿意

sentences.en: wait.

sentences.en: There is someone who's going to love you, in a way that you cannot even imagine who is going to think that you're the most perfect person, who is going to treat you
sentences.zh: 总会有人来爱你，以一种你甚至无法想象的方式，觉得你是最完美的人，会用一种

sentences.en: in a way that you have begged to be treated from every past person.
sentences.zh: 你曾向过去每一个人苦苦哀求的方式来对待你。

sentences.en: I always say this on the show, so sorry if I'm like a broken record, but I would rather find the love of my life at 35 than reach that age and realize that I had settled too soon.
sentences.zh: 我在节目里总这么说，如果我像个复读机一样请见谅，但我宁愿在35岁时找到一生的挚爱，也不愿到了那个年纪才发现自己过早地将就了。

sentences.en: Also, whatever you do, if you are still emotionally raw, do not get into a new relationship.
sentences.zh: 还有，无论你做什么，如果你内心感情依然千疮百孔，切勿开始一段新的恋情。

sentences.en: That is the number one piece of advice.
sentences.zh: 这是第一位的建议。

sentences.en: I probably should have said it sooner.

sentences.en: I know it can be so easy to use love and affection and the love and affection of another person to soothe the wounds of loss, but I promise you in the long run, it will

sentences.en: come back to bite you.
sentences.zh: 会反噬你的。

sentences.en: Take some time to be alone.

sentences.en: It's really sacred.
sentences.zh: 这真的很神圣。

sentences.en: There is going to be a point in your future, when you're married, when you have kids, whatever, where you're going to look back at this time where you were single in your
sentences.zh: 你的未来终究会迎来这样一个时刻，当你结了婚、有了孩子，无论怎样，你会回想起这段20多岁单身的时光，

sentences.en: 20s and wish that you just had one more day like that.
sentences.zh: 并且多么希望自己能再拥有这样的一天。

sentences.en: So really cherish it and I promise you will thank yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以请好好珍惜它，我向你保证你会感谢自己的。

sentences.en: You will learn so much about who you are.
sentences.zh: 你会对你是谁有深刻的了解。

sentences.en: You will discover so much about your identity and your personality through heartbreak more than you will in any relationship, more than any relationship can teach you.
sentences.zh: 通过心碎，你将对自己的身份和个性有如此多的发现，这是在任何关系中、在任何关系所能教给你的东西都无法比拟的。

sentences.en: You know, we've all been there and I know a few of you will roll your eyes when I say this.
